closure.verdict:
NOT CERTIFIABLE — but the spine holds, and most of the round-1 repairs are correct. Be clear about the split.

WHAT IS RIGHT. Every repair I could check at the site it was made says the right thing. R1/R1b: §3.10.1 now gap-ledgers crm.appointment.{attendance,duration,services,fields}.v1 under GAP-APPOINTMENT-DETAIL-COMMIT and reads «Seven of the thirteen carry policyDecision: ALLOW; three of them are allowlisted» — I executed the registry and got exactly thirteen targetKind === 'appointment' rows, seven ALLOW, with the four detail keys ALLOW and unpaired, so §3.10.1, F34, F37, F31's pairing veto and §2.6.5 now agree and the row could not load. R2/R2b/R31: DraftClass is declared once, in §0.14 F79, with the same five members the pre-repair prose carried — no member was lost — and §2.4 row 16, §2.6.16's body and SETTINGS.1 all cite it. R3 is correct where it was applied: F72 has no default branch and BOOK.2 cites it. R30/R30b, R32, R33–R33c (§4.4.3 is now exactly total over §3.7's 31 members), R34/R35 (all 22 kinds carry a retention row; MEDIA.4 cites the table), R36/R37, R38, R40/R41, R46, R47, R48 are all correct. The 19-collapse pass worked: a mechanical extraction of top-level declarations from every fenced block finds zero cross-section duplicates except the subjectCapability signature/body pair F6a explicitly admits. All five «MUST STILL HOLD» items hold — exactly two floor reductions, both in §0.17, no third clause creating one; §2.6.7 CLIENT.2 and §2.6.22 ARTIFACT.3 present and unrenumbered, with CLIENT.3 and ARTIFACT.5 additive (role fixing) and superseding nothing; Gate 5 recomputes verificationFloor from the IntentRecord and F42/§3.7 carry priority and widget_kind so the exempt branch is reproducible; Gate 6 dispatches on subjectCapability(record) and its HANDOFF branch resolves destination fences only; A0.2 declares no ordering and no precedence language survives anywhere; no normative clause cites an erratum. Every §0 cardinality is exact against the executed registries: 226 / 221 / 47 / 56, plus 129/95/2 policyDecision, 105 ALLOW+authenticated_request, 53 unreachable by source type, 98 riskFacet tokens, MONEY 92 (39 reachable), TENANT_AUTHORITY 28/14, CONSENT 3, IDENTITY 6, MARKETING_FANOUT 4, the seven autonomyLevel counts, and 19 non-test approvalRequirement: REQUIRED.

WHY IT STILL FAILS. The round repaired rules and did not walk their readers.

The one that matters is FORM.2. R3 is called the largest of the three security-contract violations, and its dependent in §2.6.17 was never opened: FORM.2 still says the canonical draft owner «returns next_envelope = SETTINGS_DRAFT (or BOOKING_CONFIRMATION for a booking-class capability, or PAYMENT_HANDOFF for a payment-class one), as BOOK.2's derivation fixes». That is the deleted two-test chain restated in prose, in a normative clause, citing a rule that now explicitly disclaims having a derivation — and FORM.2 is the clause the FORM → draft → confirmation path actually reads. Under it, 94 of the 105 widget-reachable capabilities route onto a COMMIT-bearing kind, which is the exact figure I recomputed from the registry and the exact figure F72 quotes as its reason for having no default branch. The fence was removed from one clause and left standing in another. SETTINGS.1's Mechanism sentence carries the same dangling «BOOK.2's derivation» citation.

Two more repaired rules have dependents that contradict them. §0.6 F21 — the owning declaration of the key-space rule — still carries the wide «zero capability: string declarations in the widget layer» source test that R39 narrowed at §3.2; that test fails against this contract's own §1.1.2 WidgetComposerInput.capability: string. And §3.7 R3.7.2 still states its own version of F15's erasure-reachability test over a wider gate set including Gate 8-R, whose mandated read of readback_ack.affirmation §4.4.3 classifies CONVERSATION_CONTENT — so the collapse that made §0.16 FR-12 cite F15 left the drifted, unpassable twin in place.

The cross-reference sweep is the repair that overclaims. «Normative text now cites zero unresolvable sections» is true for dangling §0.N (all of those are now confined to Annex B, which is out of scope) and false for wrong-target citations. The repair record names the §0.4 pointer as a known defect and then fixes two of four: §1.8 K8 and §3.4 R3.4.8 still send a reader to Mint classes and erasure classes for the floor derivation and the pinned floor vector. Three clauses cite «the forbidden-key list of §0.14», which is the finance fence; the list is §0.15 F88. §1.0 sends the reader to §0.2 for the eleven evaluation points, which are §0.3 F7. §1.1.1's root-member table gives origin, authority and presentation as §0.3 when §0.5 F17 declares them. §1.2 V1 cites §7, a section §0.2 F6 declares void. None of these is caught by the mechanisms this round installed, because F6's link test only asks whether the target resolves and F6a's second pass only catches self-restatement — the fault here is a valid pointer aimed at the wrong rule, and nothing tests for that.

Two defects are new, both in text R45/R46 added. §A1.7's P-27 row names FR-13 and R3.11.5 as its dependants; the clauses that actually carry a P-27 status are F90(4)/FR-6f and R3.11.6, so F35(2)'s start-up assertion over MECHANISM_GAP_LEDGER fails by construction. And §A5, rewritten in the same round that added P-23…P-32 to §A1, still tells the reader «§A1 enumerates the prerequisite components P-01 … P-22».

Everything else the closure lens asked for resolves. All eighteen distinct P-nn cited by a NORMATIVE-PENDING status (P-01, P-02, P-08, P-11, P-12, P-13, P-16, P-17, P-18, P-19, P-22, P-23…P-32) now have rows; A1.7 closes the ten that had none. No dependent went unresolved for want of evidence.

EXIT BAR. Seven edits — FORM.2, SETTINGS.1, F21's mechanism sentence, R3.7.2's path set, the eight residual mis-citations, P-27's dependants, A5's range — and this passes. FORM.2 is the only one with a live security consequence; the rest are legibility and build-test integrity. None requires reopening a rule, and none touches the authority spine.

adversarial.verdict:
SUBSTANCE LARGELY CORRECT, CLOSURE NOT ACHIEVED — NOT CERTIFIABLE.

What holds, checked and stated plainly. Every repair in block A is correct on its merits and verifiable against the executed registries. I ran the four baselines and every cardinality the repairs rest on: ActionCapabilityRegistry.list() = 226, canonicalProductionPolicyDefinitions() = 221, MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG = 47, C9_CAPABILITIES = 56 — exact. Derived figures also reproduce exactly: targetKind === 'appointment' = 13, of which 7 ALLOW (R1b's corrected reading); policyDecision ALLOW 129 / SHADOW_ONLY 95 / DENY 2; ALLOW ∧ authenticated_request = 105; 53 unreachable by source type; 98 distinct riskFacets tokens; MONEY = 92 of 226 and 39 of the 105 against 12/4 for the bare 'financial' token; CONSENT 3, IDENTITY 6, MARKETING_FANOUT 4, TENANT_AUTHORITY 28/14; autonomyLevel distribution 19/95/1/50/42/14/5; 19 non-test approvalRequirement REQUIRED; 5 kernel.test synthetics. F72's deleted chain reproduces at 118 (ALLOW ∧ ¬financial ∧ ¬appointment) and 94 of the 105 widget-reachable — R3's quantification is sound, and F72 having no default branch is the right fence. R1 is correct and was a real security-contract violation: the four appointment-detail keys are ALLOW with the twelve-role default and three carry no clientPrincipalTarget, and F31's pairing assertion would have made an allowlist row unloadable, so the gap ledger is the only consistent disposition. R2/R31's DraftClass is now a single five-member type in §0.14 F79, cited by §2.4 row 16 and §2.6.16's body, with SETTINGS.1 stating the expense/loyalty exclusion and its two grounds. R33's §4.4.3 table is total over §3.7's 31 declared members and over no others — selection_min/selection_max gone, all six missing members present. R34/R35's §4.4.2 carries all twenty-two kinds and MEDIA.4 cites it. R36/R37 moved frozen_nouns into the AUDIT_RETAINED block and keyed R3.7.2 on §4.4.3. R38's R3.1.0 is a numbered rule with a mechanism. R46 closed cleanly: every P-nn reference in §§0–4 and Annex A resolves to a row in A1.1–A1.7, P-01 through P-32, no orphan.

All five MUST-STILL-HOLD items hold. Exactly two floor reductions, both in §0.17; no clause elsewhere creates a third (§3.14 and §3.16.8 point at §0.17 without enumerating). §2.6.7 CLIENT.2 is present and unrenumbered, now stating its own validateEnvelope kind-level refusal rather than citing the undefined «display fence», with CLIENT.3 sitting beside it, not over it. §2.6.22 ARTIFACT.3 (contains_pii) is present and unrenumbered, with ARTIFACT.5 beside it. Gate 5 recomputes verificationFloor(record, record.widget_kind) from the IntentRecord and the live tables, and the record carries priority, widget_kind, body_hash, selection_domain and c9_domain for exactly that purpose. Gate 6 binds ref = subjectCapability(record) once and dispatches on it, and its HANDOFF branch resolves destination fences only — registration in space, SENSITIVE_DEST, targetFloor('s'), the landing surface's ingress — never assertCanExecute, c9Capability's domain/mode admission, or the commit allowlist. No precedence chain exists anywhere: A0.2 declares none and A1.6.2 is restated over F32/F31/F72 rather than overriding §0.21. Zero errata citations survive in normative text — I grepped every E-n/EB-n/EC-n token across lines 1–6018 and found none outside Annex B.

Why it is still not certifiable. The round repaired the rules and did not finish walking their dependents, and two repairs are wrong in a way that matters.

The worst is R39. The record says §3.2 was «wider than F21» and narrows it. But F21 — the clause §0.2's map makes the sole owner of CapabilityRef — still carries the identical wide sentence, «a source test asserts zero `capability: string` declarations in the widget layer», while R3.2.2 now carries the narrow form and says in its own text that the wide form «would also condemn `AE_WIDGET_COMMIT_ALLOWLIST`'s own string-keyed rows». F30 declares that allowlist as Record<string, AeCommitRow> with ae_key: string. So the repair fixed the copy and left the original, the owning clause now fails its own build test on a table this contract declares, and §A1.7 P-24 repeats the wide form a third time. That is a rule stated in three places in two strengths.

Second: R3.4.7 says the five-intent census «is declared in §0.8 (F48, F49) and is not restated here» — and restates it, as an unmarked normative table, in the next four lines. That is exactly the pattern §0.2 F6a's second pass is declared to fail the build on, added in this very round to catch it. The document cannot pass its own new gate.

Third: three collapses did not collapse. max_commit_intents' pairing veto went ×3 → ×2 (§2 K13 still prints it). The escape-verb rule went ×3 → ×2 (the §2.6 preamble still prints it). The forbidden-key list was never on the target list and F88's «stated once» is false against R3.8.2's thirteen-key-shorter, one-evaluation-point copy — a security-relevant fence read through two different lists by §0.12 F71 and §3.3 respectively.

Fourth, the cross-reference claim. «Normative text now cites zero errata and zero unresolvable sections» is half true. §1.2 V1 cites «§7's renderTextEquivalent» in a section-count of five that F6 closes; §1.8 K8 and §3.4 R3.4.8 both still say «declared in §0.4» for verificationFloor and C9_FLOOR_BASELINE, which is the exact §0.4→§0.8 error the record's own block D says it fixed; four clauses cite §0.14 for the forbidden-key list that lives in §0.15; §1.0 cites §0.2 for the eleven evaluation points that live in §0.3; §1.1.1 cites §0.3 six times for shapes declared in §0.5.

Fifth, the closure the brief flagged as dangerous. requiredConfirmationKind is now correct at F72 and correctly cited by BOOK.2, §3.10.1 and A1.6.2. But §3.9's Gate 7 — the sole declaration of the gate that F72, BOOK.2 and FR-6b all name as the re-check point — does not list the lookup among its checks; and SETTINGS.1 and FORM.2 still attribute the rule to «BOOK.2's derivation», at a clause that now declares it has no derivation of its own. F21 and F72 also disagree on the type of the fence's only argument.

THE OWNER'S EXIT BAR IS NOT MET. SECURITY CONTRACT VIOLATIONS: 0 — no fence is weakened in the admitting direction; the three security-contract findings of round 1 are closed and verified against the registry; the Gate 7 and F28/dispatch_is_synchronous gaps leave the mint-time refusal intact and fail closed. FUNDAMENTAL RULES: hold. STRUCTURAL VIOLATIONS: not 0 — six incorrect or incomplete repairs and six new or surviving defects above, at least three of which (R3.4.7, F21/R3.2.2, F88/R3.8.2) are contradictions between two live statements of one rule. UNPROVEN NORMATIVE CLAIMS: not 0 — F6a asserts «one place per rule» is a checked property, and the property is false in seven places, so the assertion is a claim the build would refute. «ONE DOCUMENT, ONE PLACE PER RULE»: false.

What is left is bounded and mechanical: repair F21's mechanism sentence, delete R3.4.7's restated census, collapse the three remaining duplicates, add the confirmation-kind check to Gate 7's declared checks, and run the §N.M link test F6 now specifies over normative text — roughly twenty edits, none of which changes a rule's meaning. Run F6a and the F6 link test against the document before the next certification; both would have caught every structural finding in this report.
